comment: The glimpse suite (daydream/glimpse.py; playtest 2026-09-29b): a sentence a room's description says, a thing it names that is not an object, and a verb a player tried. Scored by glimpse.valid_line; the lines go to the blind prose sheet.

cases.sentence: The lantern by the stair burns low and steady.
Shelves run along the brick walls, and on them sit rows of small glass jars, each holding a folded slip of paper: an hour somebody saved and never spent.
Paper lanterns hang from crooked poles all around the little square, each in its own warm pool of light, and moths turn slow above the cobbles.
Crooked old trees stand in a loose ring, and their round fruit glow softly, each one a small lamplit evening.
Reeds whisper along the bank, and the river goes by as slowly as a long afternoon.
The old stone bridge arches over a slow dark river, hung end to end with lanterns whose reflections sway on the water like golden fish.
Wooden pigeonholes climb every wall, and every pigeonhole holds letters: written, sealed, and never sent.
The old stone well stands cool and green with moss, ferns nodding at its foot.
One weathered bench faces east, toward a pale edge of sky that never quite decides to become morning while anyone is watching.
Lanterns hang on brackets all along the narrow lane, and the leaning houses have blue doors and window boxes full of moss.
A round window looks out over the village roofs.
